{{Quote|And this creature, this heap of fat and entrails and low cunning, this thing has made a servant of me. Worse, a slave. He degrades me, abuses me, amuses himself by abasing me. Me! Whose shadow he is not fit to touch!|Bib Fortuna talking about Jabba the Hutt|<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" />}}
'''Bib Fortuna''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] from [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. Bib served as a [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]] to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] for many years. Considering he served Jabba for that few in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] hated the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] as much as he did&mdash;the Twi'lek majordomo had tried many times unsuccessfully to have Jabba killed. A member of the [[Una Clan]], Bib Fortuna was friendly with many [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr monks]] in Jabba's Palace&mdash;when he died, his [[Brain/Legends|brain]] was forcibly removed from his body by the ancient religious order, and placed in a jar for the enlightenment process.

==Biography==
===In the service of Jabba===
====Meeting Jabba====
[[File:Ryloth_EotECR.png|thumb|right|300px|Ryloth, where Fortuna caused a planet-wide breakdown of order]]
The [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Bibfort'una was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] to the [[Una Clan|Una clan]] on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]],<ref name="TNEGC" /> where he was an ambitious entrepreneur.<ref name="SESourcebook">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref> When he was a mere [[Youngling/Legends|boy]], he traveled away from Ryloth<ref name="TNEGC" /> seeking opportunities in the larger [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="Guide">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> Bibfort'una quickly gained [[Currency/Legends|wealth]]<ref name="TNEGC" /> in his first business venture<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> trafficking contraband [[Ryll/Legends|ryll spice]]<ref name="TNEGC" /> and becoming one of its foremost exporters.<ref name="SESourcebook" /> 

This action, however, led to<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> a planet-wide breakdown of order<ref name="CSWEFortuna">{{CSWECite|I|291|Fortuna, Bib}}</ref> with drug wars,<ref name="Secrets of Tatooine" /> [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] coming to his homeworld,<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> and the Twi'lek becoming one.<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> Angered by the [[Death/Legends|death]] and slavery, a court of Bibfort'una's Twi'lek peers<ref name="TEGC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> in the Twi'lek government<ref name="Secrets of Tatooine" /> sentenced him to death, but he was able to escape with his name dishonored and his assets taken. Now removed from Ryloth culture, his personal name and his clan name were split and he was known as Bib Fortuna from that point forward.<ref name="TNEGC" /> 

Fortuna spent several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] being<ref name="TNEGC" /> a hunted criminal<ref name="SWVD" /> with a Twi'lek bounty on his head.<ref name="TEGC" /> He tried to intrude his way into the [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] corporate bureaucracy, but a noteworthy display of untrustworthiness got him removed from the group's headquarters on the planet [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]].<ref name="TMA">''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''</ref> Fortuna became a successful freelancer<ref name="TNEGC" /> though trading spice, and at one point dealt with the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. The desperate and down-on-his-luck Twi'lek used his criminal contacts to try and infiltrate the court of the Hutt,<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> who saw potential in Fortuna, as he was a survivor, excellent organizer, and someone with strong contacts in the criminal underworld.<ref name="FF60 (2014)" />

====Majordomo duties====
[[File:JabbaPromo.png|thumb|left|300px|Bib Fortuna became the majordomo of Jabba the Hutt (pictured).]]
An [[Agent/Legends|agent]] of Jabba's approached Fortuna with the offer of the Twi'lek working for the Hutt as his production and transport agent<ref name="SESourcebook" /> of [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]]<ref name="CSWEFortuna" /> shipments.<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> Fortuna would make more than he made independently by bringing in spice that would be handled by Jabba's empire. Even though there were dangers associated with the job, the pay was good and Fortuna,<ref name="SESourcebook" /> letting his greed get the best of him,<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> signed on.<ref name="SESourcebook" /> 

Jabba hired Fortuna shortly after he arrived on<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> the planet<ref name="TNEGC" /> [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Using his position of power and influence, the Twi'lek was able to quickly rise in favor of Jabba's court<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> and move through successively more prominent roles<ref name="CSWEFortuna" /> to the position of [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]] in Jabba's organization, much to the detriment of less able schemers.<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> As majordomo, he supervised the<ref name="SWVD" /> [[Local day/Legends|day]]-to-day<ref name="CharEnc" /> affairs of [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's palace]] and the<ref name="SWVD" /> [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|Desilijic Complex]]<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> in the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].<ref name="SWVD" /> Fortuna used this role to plot against Jabba, planning to take over the Hutt's business after Jabba's death.<ref name="CSWEFortuna" />

If anyone wanted to do business with Jabba, they would first have to deal with Fortuna. The Twi'lek met visitors to the Hutt's palace after the main gate's sentry systems scanned for hostility. If they were let through the gate, Fortuna would meet with them accompanied by [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] guards.<ref name="SWE">{{SWE|characters|bibfortuna|Bib Fortuna}}</ref> Fortuna gained favor with Jabba though gift-giving,<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|bibfortuna|Fortuna, Bib}}</ref> and he often hovered near Jabba's ear feeding information and giving advice. He was a firsthand witness of Jabba's most cruel and wretched doings and stood aside whenever he enslaved Twi'lek slave girls.<ref name="SWE" />

====Meeting the B'omarr monks====
While he was a new majordomo, Fortuna was hungry to learn everything about the palace, in particular the main and secret corridors, rooms, the dungeons, and the people's routines. While he was accompanying the kitchen staff on their rounds feeding prisoners one evening, a [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr monk's]] [[B'omarr brain walker|spider walker]] jumped on to the group just as they reached the first cell, causing hot [[Soup/Legends|soup]] to spill on Fortuna's [[Clothing/Legends|robes]]. Using his [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]], the Twi'lek shot the walker's [[Brain/Legends|brain]] jar, making the jar explode and the brain to fall to the floor. When the walker short-circuited, Fortuna finally realized the spider walker was mechanical. Monks rushed to collect the brain and placed it in a nutrient jar wherein which it could contemplate the cosmos.<ref name="Bib's Tale" /> 

[[File:BomarrBrainWalker-ROTJ.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A B'omarr brain walker (pictured) jumped on Fortuna.]]
Gagging at the thought of the brain contemplating in the jar, Fortuna rushed back to the palace throne room to advise Jabba to have the B'omarr order exterminated. He was astonished at the idea of two distinct cultures&mdash;the monks and Jabba's empire&mdash;lived in the palace. Stopping on his way to Jabba, Fortuna thought about how he was angry that the monks resided in the palace, and how they must feel about Jabba and his minions. The majordomo then realized he could use their discontent to his advantage by siding with them in their complaints, pretending to learn from them, guide them into open plotting against the Hutt, and mold them an unsuspected force he could call upon when he took control of Jabba's organization.<ref name="Bib's Tale" /> 

====Demoted to errand boy====
After mishandling a petty triviality around the time of the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]<ref name="TNEGC" /> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="32 BBY">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}} to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> Fortuna was demoted to the rank of errand boy and replaced as majordomo by [[Naroon Cuthus]]. Now stuck in his employ without the influence he once had, Fortuna began to hate Jabba more than he hated his Twi'lek brethren.<ref name="TNEGC" />

[[File:Bib_TPM.png|thumb|left|300px|Fortuna and Jabba attend the Boonta Eve Classic.]]
Fortuna attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] of [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] with his employer, who hosted the event. He stood at Jabba's side through the Hutt's welcome to all the contestants and spectators who attended the event. He witnessed [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] win the race, securing the young boy's freedom from a life of [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]]. At the conclusion of the race, he was forced to wake Jabba, who had fallen asleep sometime after the second lap.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>

At some point, he returned to [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] seeking his revenge and ransacking seven [[City/Legends|cities]], capturing most members and selling them into slavery for Jabba. While finding loot for himself he came across [[Nat Secura]] and his mother, who chastised him for his actions, cursing his name. The insult resulted in Fortuna executing her and taking Secura under his wing, though he was horribly scarred. Fortuna only took Secura as a way to take over Ryloth for himself in the future, using the good name of [[Clan Secura]].<ref name="Bib's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Of the Day's Annoyances: Bib Fortuna's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

====The Clone Wars====
{{Quote|I have your attention. You will take me to your master now.''"<br />"''You&hellip; have&hellip; my attention&hellip; my m-master? ''[&hellip;]'' My master is not here. He is far away.''"<br />"''Then who is in charge of operations here? Who do you report to?''"<br />"''&hellip;My master is in charge&hellip;|Keelyvine Reus and Bib Fortuna|<ref name="Valsedian Operation">''[[The Clone Wars: The Valsedian Operation]]''</ref>}}
In [[22 BBY/Legends|21.95 BBY]], one month into the galactic conflict known as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the [[Hunt for the Decimator]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|21.95 BBY]]</ref> one of Jabba's rivals, a Hutt named [[Boorka]], began an alliance with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Jabba sought to eliminate Boorka, and arranged a meeting with the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Echuu Shen-Jon]], which Fortuna was present for.<ref name="CC">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref>

During the [[21 BBY/Legends|first year]] of the Clone Wars,<ref name="SW Annual 2011">''[[Star Wars Annual 2011]]''</ref> the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] set up a secret mining facility on the [[Ore/Legends|ore]]-rich [[Valsedian asteroid belt]], deep inside [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. It was there that the [[Gender/Legends|male]] Twi'lek worked, likely in a position of administrator. While the facility was very isolated, the Separatist operations there did not go unnoticed; Jabba learned about it, and suspected that it was sold to the Confederacy by his distant cousin, [[Torpo]]. This violated the terms of a treaty between the Hutts and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], and Jabba informed the Republic of the situation, which led to a team of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] being sent to [[Mission to the Valsedian asteroid belt|investigate the asteroid belt]] to ascertain the existence of the mining installation.<ref name="Valsedian Operation" />

The Twi'lek administrator was working with a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] while walking near the entrance of the facility exactly at the time when [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Keelyvine Reus]] entered the base. Reus acted quickly, captured the flinched Twi'lek and used a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] on him, ordering him to take the Jedi to his master. However, the administrator revealed that his master was not anywhere near the asteroid belt. Before the interrogation could continue, Kenobi [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] that the team's [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] members, who had taken an alternate route inside the facility, were in danger and rushed to aid them. Reus bound the Twi'lek at the nearby tubes with [[Stuncuffs/Legends|stun cuffs]], and questioned him more closely. She suspected that Torpo was the master of the administrator, and asked about the whereabouts of the Hutt. The Twi'lek confused the Jedi by stating that while his master was gone, Torpo was inside the facility. Before Reus could learn more, she was suddenly attacked by Confederacy [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], who challenged her to a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]]. The pair engaged each other, leaving the still-bound Twi'lek behind.<ref name="Valsedian Operation" />

====Fortuna's assassination plot====
=====Meeting with Gaar Suppoon=====
{{Quote|The trip will be worth it. You could learn from this.''"<br />"''Yes, your excellency. But I presume to hope it will a short visit?''"<br />"''No, this is a jubjub, a business ceremony, He'll have some entertainment planned. We can't rush him.|Jabba and Bib Fortuna while approaching Suppoon's palace|<ref name="GaarSuppoon">''[[Jabba the Hutt: The Gaar Suppoon Hit]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Jth_tgsh.jpg|thumb|300px|right|Jabba and Fortuna visited Suppoon's planet to conduct a jubjub.]]
By [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]],<ref name="DHCT">The date of ''[[Jabba the Hutt: The Gaar Suppoon Hit]]'' is established by {{DarkHorse|url=Zones/StarWars/Timeline|text=Comics Timeline}} in relation to {{Film|IV}}, which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].</ref> Fortuna planned to subdue with drugs Jabba and torture him to acquire his secrets. To help in his efforts, he enlisted [[Nivek (criminal)|Nivek]],<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal">''[[Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal]]''</ref> a humanoid follower of Jabba's,<ref name="Nivek">{{CSWECite|II|384|Nivek}}</ref> to recruit and arm other helpers.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" /> That year,<ref name="DHCT" /> the Twi'lek, Jabba, and his entourage traveled on the ''Star Jewel'' to the [[Suppoon's planet|planet]] of the [[Gaar (title)|Gaar]] [[Suppoon]],<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> a [[Bah'r Kilido]] criminal kingpin<ref name="BarelyTolerable">{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-1|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref> and rival of Jabba's,<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> to conduct a highly illigal<ref name="FF49">{{FactFile|49|JAB 5-8|Jabba the Hutt}}</ref> [[jubjub]], a business ceremony.<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> The ceremony was desired by Suppoon despite Jabba's warning of planting a bomb at the Gaar's palace to ensure no double-crossing.<ref name="FF49" /> 

For trade, Jabba brought along the<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> infamous scientist<ref name="FF49" /> [[Pineas Pontak]] with his disembodied brain,<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> and a biologically engineered [[Pontak Hypergland|hypergland]] from the scientist's laboratories. The Hutt seemingly wanted to trade the hypergland for a female [[tromonid]] but actually wanted a male tromonid so he could breed the creatures and harvest the poison created by them.<ref name="FF49" /> Before the visit, Fortuna and bet one hundred credits that he would return from the trip with Jabba's second-in-command, [[Scuppa]].<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi">''[[Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi]]''</ref>

As the group made their way to [[Suppoon's palace]], Fortuna mentioned to Jabba that he hoped the Gaar would appreciate the visit. The Hutt responded back that the trip would be worthwhile, and Fortuna could learn from it. The Twi'lek then asked if the visit would be short and Jabba replyed with an explanation of a jubjub and that they couldn't rush the Gaar. Now inside the palace, Jabba and Suppoon bet on a fighting match between two creatures. After the match was over, Fortuna, The Hutt, his entourage, and Suppoon moved to a table to get to business. At the table, Suppoon confronted Jabba about the supposed bomb he had placed within the Bah'r Kilido's palace.<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> [[Kosh Kurp]], an Imperial security expert employed by Suppoon,<ref name="FF49" /> had not found any bomb. Jabba was adamant that he did place a bomb and the two dropped the topic and began business.<ref name="GaarSuppoon" />

=====Tromonoid trade=====
{{Quote|Don't think I didn't notice how ready you were to jump ship when it looked like he had me, you jelly-eyed traitor! Watch yourself, Bib. I could learn to distrust you.''"<br />"''But I&mdash;''"<br />"''No "buts," Bib...|Jabba and Bib Fortuna while exiting Suppoon's palace|<ref name="GaarSuppoon" />}}
A servant of Suppoon's brought out a female tromonid and Fortuna brought out the hypergland. Suppoon had wanted more&mdash;Pontak himself<ref name="GaarSuppoon" />&mdash;which Jabba anticipated.<ref name="FF49" /> The Gaar was lied to about Pontak's condition and was unaware that his brain had been removed. Fortuna brought out the scientist and removed the covering over his face. Jabba traded the scientist for a male tromonid, but the tromonoid turned out to be irritated<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> with radiation burn.<ref name="FF49" /> Angered at this, Jabba had Fortuna bring out the brain of Pontak, which led to the Hutt's life being threatened by a henchman hanging from a roof affixture.<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> Keeping cool,<ref name="FF49" /> Jabba opened up the cage of the female tromonoid, which Suppoon took back. Escaping from the cage, the tromonoid latched onto the Gaar's arm and inflicted a soon lethal bite. Jabba offered a syringe of [[tromonoid antidote]], which he took from Fortuna, to Suppoon. Having no choice with the bomb Jabba was now holding over him, the Bah'r Kilido took the syringe without trouble and agreed to Jabba's new demands of spice.<ref name="GaarSuppoon" />

[[File:SuppoonDeath-TheGaarSuppoonHit.png|thumb|left|300px|Suppoon was killed when Kosh Kurp turned on him.]]
Jabba then tried to leave, but Suppoon had Kosh Kurp take Jabba's bomb and detonate it. The Gaar then ordered to Jabba's entourage to surrender if they wanted to live.<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> Fortuna, seeking safety, surrendered to who would be his new master,<ref name="FF60 (2014)"> {{FactFile2014|60|FOR 1-4|Bib Fortuna}}</ref> but Jabba did not back down. Jabba reminded Suppoon that he still had the original bomb he left inside his palace. Suppoon called his bluff, and the Hutt adressed him as "Sonopo Bomoor," the alias the Gaar used when he governed the<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> planet<ref name="BarelyTolerable" /> of [[Intuci]]. There, Suppoon sacked the<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> city<ref name="BarelyTolerable" /> [[Bonaka Nueno]] and massacred Kurp's family. Now realizing the Gaar was the leader who affected his life greatly, the security expert turned on Suppoon. Kurp advanced on Suppoon, who threatened to shoot<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> him.<ref name="BarelyTolerable" /> The Bah'r Kilido finally shot, but the bolt reflected off of<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> Kurp's [[Man-o'-war body armor|armor]]<ref name="BarelyTolerable" /> back towards him, separating Suppoon's head from his body. Jabba instated Kurp as the leader of the late Gaar's servants and he and his group left the palace. While on the way out, the Twi'lek complimented Jabba's handling of the situation but the Hutt told him he noticed Fortuna ready to surrender and reminded him that he worked for him. The group then took off in the ''Star Jewel''<ref name="GaarSuppoon" /> to Tatooine.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" />

=====Captured by the Princess of Orooturoo=====
{{Quote|What has she to gain from killing us all? I'm certain that if we show her we are willing to serve her, she will find it to her advantage to let us live.''"<br />"''Bib, your pragmatism is distictly admirable.|Bib Fortuna, plotting with two guards, and Jabba|<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" />}}
[[File:BibFortunaNuffin-JtH-AotD.png|thumb|right|350px|Fortuna impersonates a Nuffin]]
On the ship, Jabba ordered Fortuna to oversee the storage of the various things acquired during Jabba's visit to the Gaar Suppoon's planet. While in space, the Star Jewel came across a [[Nuffin freighter]] used by the [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Nampi]] of<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" /> the planet<ref name="Orooturoo">{{CSWECite|II|424|Orooturoo}}</ref> [[Orooturoo]] as a trap.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" /> Sensing a profit,<ref name="FF58">{{FactFile|58|JAB 9-12|Jabba the Hutt}}</ref> Jabba had Fortuna vocally impersonate a member of a [[Nuffin]] trade team who had commandeered a pirate spacecraft while a hologram of a Nuffin acted as a visual representation. A [[Unidentified Nuffin|Nuffin]] enslaved by Nampi responded and asked Fortuna to explain himself and revealed that the freighter's pulse rockets were trained on the ''Star Jewel''. Fortuna lied that his trade team was waylaid by privateers in the [[Ampuroon]] mining district of<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" /> the planet<ref name="Waskiro">{{CSWECite|III|321|Waskiro}}</ref> [[Waskiro/Legends|Waskiro]] yet he and his team were able to escape because they used [[LBK]]'s and escaped in the ''Star Jewel''. Curious about the LBK's, the Nuffin inquired about the state of them. Fortuna explained that they were prototypes but still helpful. The Nuffin congratulated Fortuna then asked if Twi'lek needed anything, Fortuna saying fuel and medical attention. The Nuffin then let the ''Star Jewel'' dock with the freighter. Jabba complemented the Twi'lek on his impersonation.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" />

[[File:JabbafreesFortuna-JtH-AotD.png|thumb|left|350px|Jabba freed Fortuna after Nampi's death.]]
Fortuna, Jabba, Scuppa, and two guards boarded the ship, not aware it was not a Nuffin freighter and were greeted with the forces of Nampi. The door behind them closed and the group surrendered. Jabba and Scuppa were taken to meet the Princess and Fortuna and the two guards were taken into custody. Jabba would not let Nampi take the treasure on the ''Star Jewel'' and was too imprisoned. Scuppa tried to talk the Hutt into letting Nampi take his treasure, but that only angered Jabba. After sweet-talking the Princess, Scuppa became the husband of Nampi. She then proceeded to eat him,<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" /> like all her prospective husbands.<ref name="FF58" /> Unbeknownst to her, she had ingested a remote-activated vial of [[Xenoboric acid/Legends|xenoboric acid]] implanted by Jabba into Scuppa's brain as a security measure. Jabba offered the hungry princess some of his treasure to not be killed and the princess agreed. After killing two of Nampi's guards with the ''Star Jewel's'' defense system, Jabba retrieved the remote control to the acid and used it to kill Nampi. The Hutt then went to free Fortuna and the two guards,<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: The Hunger of Princess Nampi" /> finding the Twi'lek plotting treachery with his guards. Jabba was focused on loading his new treasure, however.<ref name="FF58" />

After the treasure from Nampi's Nuffin freighter was brought onto the ''Star Jewel'', Fortuna brought this news to Jabba, but their attention was redirected to the late Princess' forces. Fortuna suggested they bring the Nuffin freighter to the nearby<ref name="JHDT">''[[Jabba the Hutt: The Dynasty Trap]]''</ref> planet<ref name="Smarteel">{{CSWECite|III|169|Smarteel}}</ref> [[Smarteel]] and gift the ship<ref name="JHDT" /> to criminal business associate<ref name="Smarteel" /> [[Cabrool Nuum]]. Jabba complimented the idea and, feeling good about himself, killed Nampi's forces by expelling them through an airlock. The ''Star Jewel'' landed on Smarteel and Jabba exited while ordering Fortuna to stay with the ship. After a series of betrayals from Nuum's family which left them dead at the hands of Jabba, he returned to his ship.<ref name="JHDT" />

=====Enacting the betrayal=====
{{Quote|Hate? What a tiny, insignificant, useless word. What I feel for Jabba can only be expressed by causing every nerve in his body to experience the greatest possible pain for the longest possible time. Every moment I spend in his company is an eternity of loathing. The overpowering stench that pours from his open mouth, the sight of his thick, greasy, pustule-covered flesh, his unspeakable acts of depravity... He is the most revolting monster in the galaxy!|Bib Fortuna on Jabba|<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" />}}
[[File:BibFortunasRecruits-JtH-AotD.png|thumb|right|350px|Bib Fortuna instructs his recruits]]
Now back on Tatooine, Jabba and Fortuna looked out a window on the Star Jewel. Jabba reminisced on his many adventures and mentioned to Fortuna that their recent one had left him tired<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" />&mdash;something that Fortuna had worked hard to ensure.<ref name="FF94">{{FactFile|94|JAB 19-24|Jabba the Hutt}}</ref> Back at the palace, the Twi'lek directed a servant to either find or make room in the palace's treasure hold and then left under the false pretense of surveying the palace.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" /> 

Fortuna made his way through the palace corridors and found a nervous Nivek. After assuring him about the safety of their plot, Fortuna was led by Nivek to six individuals he was able to recruit into the betrayal plot. Fortuna went over his plans with the recruits and made sure to note how imperative it was to keep Jabba alive. One of the recruits then questioned how Fortuna could be certain Jabba was unaware of his plot, but Fortuna explained this away with how Jabba had no reason to suspect his faithful servant. Another enlistee asked if Fortuna planned on ransoming the Hutt and Fortuna clarified his plans of torturing Jabba to learn his many secrets. That same enlistee commented how it sounded like Fortuna hated Jabba more than them, causing Fortuna to go on a tangent of the many reasons he loathed his Hutt boss. The Twi'lek ordered his recruits to stay where they were, and Fortuna left to go wait for Jabba to drowse.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" /> 

[[File:RopplesBlaster-JtH-AotD.png|thumb|left|250px|Fortuna frames Gru'um Ropple]]
Now back at the throne room, Fortuna found Jabba in the company of an old friend and a new acquaintance; smuggler [[Gru'um Ropple]] and the mysterious woman [[Miramba]]. Ropple, like Fortuna, planned an assassination on the Hutt as well, using Miramba, who was actually a droid, to transport [[frecker]]s into the palace.<ref name="FF94" /> Thinking he surveyed the palace, Jabba asked if everything was as it should be. Fortuna lied and said it was, and the Hutt ordered him to get more drinks for his guests. On the way out of the room, Fortuna pawned off his duty on a servant. Going through a corridor, Fortuna met up again with Nivek and asked for a blaster. The humanoid asked if it was time, but Fortuna made it clear he was just dealing with a minor setback. Going back to the throne room, Fortuna asked if he could hang up a rag Ropple was sitting on though the smuggler told him not to bother. Lifting up the rag, Fortuna dropped Nivek's smuggled blaster, making it appear like it had fallen out of Ropple's robes. Jabba ordered Ropple and Miramba to be taken away and fed to the Great Pit of Carkoon, despite the smuggler's pleas of innocence. Jabba then told Fortuna he was going to go to sleep and the Twi'lek left to return to his recruits.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" />

=====Plot: foiled=====
{{Quote|I never knew how loyal you are, Bib. I thought you might have been... Biding your time... Didn't trust you.''"<br />"''I... You... Uh.''"<br />"''You killed like a champion for me. Risked your life. I won't forget this.|Jabba and Bib Fortuna|<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" />}}
[[File:Jabba_attack.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Freckers released by Miramba to kill Jabba foiled Fortuna's own plot to kill the Hutt.]]
Now back with Nivek and the others, Fortuna declared it was time to start the assassination and instructed them to stay single file behind him. While on the way to the throne room, one of the alien recruits got distracted and was left behind, but made their way to the cell where Miramba and Ropple were held. The recruit discovered Ropple's plot to kill Jabba and witness Miramba releasing the freckers into the palace. The recruit called out for Fortuna, who pulled out a blaster on the alien. The recruit tried to explain themself, but before they could finish, the alien was cut off by a scream from further in the palace.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" />  

Knowing that he needed the Hutt's account numbers and passwords,<ref name="FF94" /> Fortuna and his recruits stepped in and defended Jabba from the freckers. While trying to pull a frecker off of Jabba, one jumped onto Fortuna's forehead, but the Hutt was able to shoot them off. Nivek, being attacked by a frecker, was shot in the head by Fortuna after trying to abandon the plan. After the fighting settled, the Twi'lek spotted a frecker and chased after it, being led to Ropple's cell. The Twi'lek shot the frecker and angerly accused Ropple of the plot. The smuggler pleaded for Fortuna to let them work together and take Jabba's empire, but the Twi'lek stated he had a better idea; torturing Ropple and throwing him into the Great Pit of Carkoon. While leaving, Fortuna ignored Ropple and told him he had caught the Twi'lek in an unfortunate mood.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" /> 

Returning to the throne room, Jabba,<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" /> touched by Fortuna's loyalty,<ref name="FF94" /> asked where the freckers originated and Fortuna explained that Miramba how carried them. Jabba told Fortuna he thought that he was biding his time, but he killed "like a champion" for the Hutt and that he wouldn't forget the Twi'lek risking his life for him. Jabba then stated that it was just him and Fortuna, which the Twi'lek agreed with.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal" /> 

====Serving Jabba post-assassination attempt====
=====Jabba's new companion=====
[[File:Kwerve_shooting.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Moments before Fortuna and Kwerve get Jabba's lunch thrown at them]]
During or after [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="TCFHDate">"[[This Crumb for Hire]]" is set after [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] acquires the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], which occurs in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] per ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]].''</ref> Jabba, Fortuna, and Kwerve met with Han Solo and Chewbacca on [[Kwenn Space Station/Legends|Kwenn Space Station]]. Meeting under the agreement that the he Hutt would be alone, Solo was displeased to find Fortuna and Kwerve with him. An angry Kwerve pulled a blaster on the smuggler, but was disarmed by Chewbacca. While the Solo and the Wookiee left, the [[Kowakian monkey-lizard/Legends|Kowakian monkey-lizard]] [[Salacious B. Crumb/Legends|Salacious B. Crumb]] found refuge aboard the Star Jewel. Kwerve tried to get Jabba to kill the smuggler, but the Hutt told him to load spice aboard his star yacht. Fortuna attempted to ask Jabba something, but the crime lord grew mad and again told his subordinates to load the spice.<ref name="ThisCrumb">{{StoryCite|story=This Crumb for Hire|book=Wikipedia:List_of_Dark_Horse_Comics_publications|A Decade of Dark Horse 2|bformatted=''A Decade of Dark Horse'' 2}}</ref> 

As the Star Jewel set off towards Tatooine, Jabba reprimanded Fortuna and Kwerve for not keeping Chewbacca in sight and told him he would be contemplating their punishments during his lunch. Upon getting to his dish, the Hutt discovered Crumb inside. Finding their way to the Hutt, the majordomo candidates found the monkey lizard on a ceiling beam. Kwerve nearly fired at Crumb, and even though tried Fortuna to warn him, the two ended up with Jabba's lunch on themselves, making the Hutt laugh.<ref name="ThisCrumb" /> The monkey-lizard was captured by Fortuna<ref name="CharEnc" /> and then held an audience with Jabba. After spending a few hours with Crumb, the crime lord gave him a job: make him laugh or be killed.<ref name="ThisCrumb" />

=====Dyadworms for Jabba=====
{{Quote|What is your price?''"<br />"''One hundred credits.''"<br />"''One hundred is too much!''"<br />"''Oh well, there are other buyers.|Bib Fortuna and Han Solo|<ref name="Fire Ring Race">''[[Adventures in Hyperspace: Fire Ring Race]]''</ref>}}
[[File:JabbaDockingBay94-AiHFRR.png|thumb|right|350px|Jabba and Bib Fortuna met with Han Solo at Docking Bay 94.]]
Around 2 BBY,<ref name="FRR and SS Date">[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] acquires the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] per ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''. Solo has the ''Millenium Falcon'' in both ''[[Adventures in Hyperspace: Fire Ring Race]]'' and ''[[Adventures in Hyperspace: Shinbone Showdown]]'', meaning that those stories must take place during or after 2 BBY.</ref> Fortuna, Jabba, and three of his bodyguards met up with Solo and Chewbacca at Docking Bay 94 in Mos Eisley. The Human smuggler gifted the Hutt a barrel full of [[dyadworm]]s. Fortuna, looking at Solo, asked where he got the worms. Solo dodged the question and gave his price of one hundred credits. Nervously, Fortuna stated that the price was too much. Solo shrugged and said there were other buyers, causing Jabba to laugh and offer seventy credits for the barrel and an extra ten credits if Solo told him where he got them. The two continued to barter and landed on the price of ninety credits, which Fortuna paid him.<ref name="Fire Ring Race" />

With the worms now loaded onto a repulsor sled, Jabba offered Solo a job of picking up a container of [[Lashaa silk/Legends|Lashaa silk]] for two thousand credits in advance. The two agreed and Jabba made Fortuna to give Solo the credits and the data on the cargo. Fortuna paid the smuggler and handed him a datacard that had the location of the silk, [[Fornax Station]], and the passcode for the storage locker it was located in. Jabba ordered Fortuna to come along, and Jabba's forces left the docking bay. Despite being framed for stealing the [[Margravine]] [[Abominelle]]'s [[Tyrian shimmersilk/Legends|Tyrian]] [[Shimmersilk/Legends|shimmersilk]] dress while there, the two smugglers were able to travel back to Tatooine with the Lashaa silk.<ref name="Fire Ring Race" />

=====Attending Jabba's arena=====
{{Quote|I tell you the payment! You will accept! No haggling!''"<br />"''I'd better warn you, Jabba, my price goes up if Brain-tails doesn't start using mouthwash.|Bib Fortuna and Han Solo|<ref name="Shinbone Showdown">''[[Adventures in Hyperspace: Shinbone Showdown]]''</ref>}}
[[File:BibandHan-AiHSS-.png|thumb|left|250px|Han Solo found Bib Fortuna's breath displeasing.]]
Sometime after the dyadworm delivery, Fortuna, Jabba, two Gamorrean guards, and various others attended a fighting match between a [[Gundark/Legends|gundark]] and a [[Squill (creature)|squill]] at Jabba's arena in the Desilijic Complex in Mos Eisley. Jabba, the guards, and Fortuna viewed the match from the private box, though Fortuna lurked in shadows at the back of the box. Jabba invited Solo and Chewbacca to talk business and the two arrived at the box, brushing past Fortuna. The Hutt appointed the smugglers to pick up new guards and a large supply of food for the Hutt on the planet [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]].<ref name="Shinbone Showdown" />

Recognizing Gamorreans don't encourage visitors, Jabba also gave them his best translator. The crime lord signaled for Fortuna to come over and Fortuna moved beside Han and held out a datacard, which Solo ignored. He then asked Jabba about the job's price and Fortuna, not liking to be ignored, leaned toward Solo and told the smuggler to answer to him about pricing. Solo jokingly remarked to Jabba that his price would go up if "Brain-tails" didn't start using mouthwash, causing Fortuna to check his breath in embarrassment. Jabba then gave Solo another job, a long haul to Wild Space, for him to do after his Gamorr visit. The smuggler took the datacard and then asked for three thousand credits for expenses. Jabba nodded to Fortuna and the Twi'lek gave him the credits, but while doing so, made an ill-mannered remark about Solo. The smuggler made one back and told Chewbacca to come with him, but before the Wookiee did, he snarled at Fortuna to get him to jump. The pair then left and were able get the food and guards with the help of their translator [[TC-72]].<ref name="Shinbone Showdown" />

The day after, Fortuna, Jabba, and TC-72 attended a fighting match at the arena between the gundark and a group of unusually large womp rats. Solo and Chewbacca returned to box and the former began inquiring to Jabba about the previously mentioned Wild Space job, but the crime lord pressed him for the fee Solo should have paid for doing business with his contacts. Jabba let the fee be deducted from his pay for his Wild Space job, which was delivering seeds to the planet [[Shinbone]] and take back some gems for the Hutt. Fortuna gave him a new datacard and the pair left and traveled to Shinbone. The two were able to uncover [[Torkil Mux/Legends|Torkil Mux]], the Arcona overseeing Jabba's mining operation on Shinbone, keeping jewels for himself. They found this out with the help of a [[Shorty (laborer)|member]] of a [[Unidentified walking plant species|walking plant species]] being grown to be used as laborers&mdash;an idea that was Fortuna's. When the smugglers returned, Solo lied about what happened and feigned ignorance about knowing the nature of the laborers. Jabba revealed to them it was Fortuna's idea and ordered him to pay Solo one credit for returning more gems than originally asked.<ref name="Shinbone Showdown" />

=====Jabba's happy birthday=====
{{Dialogue|Bib Fortuna|&laquo;I shall be satisfied with the majordomo position. As Bidlo Kwerve has pointed out, he performed the greatest service to you. Please allow him to have the greater honor.&raquo;|Jabba|&laquo;Good.&raquo;|Bidlo Kwerve|What did he say?|Jabba|&laquo;You shall be the first victim I feed to my rancor, I will watch your struggles and remember them for all time.&raquo;|attr=Bib Fortuna makes Bidlo Kwerve, who did not understand Huttese, the first victim of Jabba's rancor|src=<ref name="Malakili's Tale" />}}
[[File:Rancor-CHRON.png|thumb|right|300px|Bidlo Kwerve stunned a rancor that would later be Jabba's (pictured).]]
After learning about the wreck of Captain [[Grizzid|Grizzid's]] light freighter in the Dune Sea and the creature that lived inside of it, Kwerve set out the next day to acquire the monster for Jabba's upcoming [[Birthday/Legends|birthday]]. Fortuna questioned him on it, but Kwerve was able to put him off with a story of [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]] hunting, which Fortuna hated. After a skirmish with the monster, that was actually a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]], it was left unconscious on top of the ship's wrecked cargo.<ref name="RancorTatooine" /> Arriving at the scene just as Kwerve subdued the rancor,<ref name="SESourcebook" /> Fortuna called outside the wreckage, demanding to know what was going on.<ref name="RancorTatooine">{{WEGCite|story=A Rancor Comes to Tatooine|book=The Star Wars Sourcebook|reprint=1}}</ref> Knowing that bringing the rancor to Jabba would win him high praise and great rewards,<ref name="FF60 (2014)" /> the Twi'lek was able to extort the Corellian into sharing the credit.<ref name="SESourcebook" /> The rancor, in its stunned state, was then captured and placed in the palace dungeons.<ref name="Malakili's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=A Boy and His Monster: The Rancor Keeper's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

The day before Jabba's birthday, the Hutt was off away on business but would be returning back to his palace the next day. [[Malakili/Legends|Malakili]], a professional monster trainer had been purchased by Fortuna and Kwerve from the traveling show [[Circus Horrificus/Legends|Circus Horrificus]] and sent to Tatooine. The trainer met with the two men at a spire on the palace grounds. After exiting the spire, Fortuna introduced himself and Kwerve to Malakili before explaining the circumstances of the monster's discovery and its usage as a birthday gift. Malakili asked the the Twi'lek why he was chosen, who reminded the trainer of his record of spending seven seasons with the Circus Horrificus. Malakili stated he liked the monsters, causing Fortuna to add that he would love the one in the palace. In the palace's lower dungeons, Malakili first saw the rancor while Fortuna and Kwerve stayed in the shadows. The trainer cried at the sight and told Fortuna that the monster was a rancor, and that he never dreamed he would be lucky enough to see one in his lifetime. The Twi'lek told Malakili that he wouldn't be just seeing it, but that the pet was his and that he would be taking care of it. The trainer then looked at the two men and told them he would do that to the best of his ability.<ref name="Malakili's Tale" />

[[File:Malakili_SWCT.png|thumb|left|200px|Malakili served as the rancor's keeper.]]
Three days after the rancor's capture,<ref name="RancorTatooine" /> after Jabba had returned to his palace, Fortuna and Kwerve, with Malakili standing behind them, congratulated the Hutt on his birthday. Fortuna introduced the gift, then introduced its keeper and gestured behind him. After they saw that Jabba was pleased with his gift, both Fortuna and Kwerve relaxed their tense shoulders. The Corellian then stepped forward and told the Hutt that he performed the actual capture. After Jabba sat up quickly, Fortuna waved his hands frantically to exercise damage control and explained that he performed the administrative details. The Twi'lek then explained how the new trapdoor he and Kwerve had installed in front of his dais worked before Jabba stated that he was pleased. He continued that he would reward his lieutenants greatly; one would become his majordomo and the other would have a greater reward that "history would remember." Fortuna, seemingly tense to Malakili, bowed and told Jabba that he would be satisfied with the majordomo role as Kwerve did the greater service, causing Kwerve, who did not understand Huttese, to give a suspicious glance at the Twi'lek. Fortuna gestured him forward and stepped back before Jabba stated that Kwerve would be the first victim of the rancor. The Corellian looked over to Fortuna, clearly not understanding Jabba. The Hutt then released the trapdoor and Kwerve was eaten.<ref name="Malakili's Tale" />

====End of Jabba's empire====
In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> Bib Fortuna recruited the [[Wayfar spies]] to watch for [[Romo Vax]] because he suspected the man of double-crossing Jabba's organization. Fortuna later ordered Vax's assassination when he discovered the man to be a [[Sennex]] spy.<ref name="SWG:JPBF">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Jabba's Palace : Bib Fortuna|Tatooine}}</ref> In the meantime, Bib Fortuna was associated with the [[White Thranta Shipping Company]], a front for illegal activities of Jabba the Hutt's criminal organization.<ref name="SWG:DI">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Digital Infection|Tatooine}}</ref>

When an undercover [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|ISB]] agent infiltrated Jabba's Palace by posing as a smuggler, it wasn't long before Fortuna approached him in the main hall and invited the agent to his personal office. There, he invited the "smuggler" to talk about his experience. However, the undercover identity was not good enough for someone as deep in the business as Fortuna. He soon realized that his collocutor was lying and ordered the guard to toss him to the rancor. The intruder, however, fought his way out and escaped.<ref name="Agents of Deception" />

[[File:BibFortunaJabba-CGSWG.png|thumb|left|220px|Bib Fortuna serving as Jabba's majordomo]]

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] Fortuna had procured the services of a dancer called [[Oola/Legends|Oola]], a naïve Twi'lek girl who was partnered with another girl called [[Sienn'rha]]. The two were being taken to Jabba's palace by a thug called [[Jerris Rudd]] when they were intercepted by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], who killed Rudd and freed Sienn, but Oola refused to go, wanting to see what life was like in the palace. Skywalker and Fortuna shared a brief conversation where Skywalker told Fortuna that his way of life was wrong and his depredations on his own people would only lead to ruin. He promised that the Rebel Alliance could protect Ryloth from the Empire, and for a moment, Fortuna strongly considered the young Jedi's words. But reality took a grip, and Fortuna dismissed Skywalker's offer. As Oola was willing to return to Jabba's palace with Fortuna, Skywalker let the two go.

Bib Fortuna's role at the palace included receiving visitors. [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] encountered Fortuna when they arrived with a gift for Jabba. Fortuna demanded they give the gift to him, but the droids insisted they were to present the gift to Jabba personally. Fortuna acquiesced and led them into the throne room, where R2-D2 played Jabba a message from Luke Skywalker. Skywalker requested that Jabba bargain for the body of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], encased in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]. Skywalker's gift was the two droids themselves. Jabba refused to bargain, but kept the droids.<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

[[File:JessAndBib-SWRPG2E.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Jess, Bib Fortuna and Salacious B. Crumb]]

Soon after, Bib was seen in the company of Jess during the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band's]] peformance of [[Jedi Rocks/Legends|Jedi Rocks]]. She stroked his [[Lekku/Legends|lekku]]<ref name="ROTJ" /> and he reciprocated the gesture in leading her by the hand around the throne room.<ref name="ROTJ" /> She was again seen in Bib's company when the dancing girl Oola was fed to [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|the rancor]]. Bib later left the musician to slumber alone on [[Jabba the Hutt's dais/Legends|Jabba's dais]], as he lay in wait with his master, ready to spring the trap as [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], disguised as [[Boushh/Legends|Boushh]], released Han Solo from the carbonite.<ref name="ROTJ" />

After the unsuccessful attempt by [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] Leia Organa to free Han Solo, Luke Skywalker came to the palace. Fortuna was given orders that he was not to be admitted. Jabba did not foresee, however, that his majordomo would be weak-minded enough to fall for his [[Mind trick/Legends|Jedi mind tricks]]. After Fortuna led Skywalker to Jabba, Jabba became furious at Fortuna and knocked him off his throne. When Skywalker defeated Jabba's rancor, he, Han Solo and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] were sentenced to be thrown into the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]]. Bib Fortuna accompanied Jabba the Hutt to the executions on [[Khetanna/Legends|his Sail Barge]]. The Jedi and his friends proved more than Jabba's forces could handle and as such, his Barge was destroyed.<ref name="ROTJ" />

===After Jabba's death===
[[File:XWRS10BT2-FC.jpg|thumb|Bib Fortuna in his [[B'omarr brain walker|"B'omarr walker"]] with [[Firith Olan]]]]

As Jabba's [[Sail barge/Legends|sail barge]] exploded, Fortuna escaped on a private skiff and returned to the palace to take over. He fought a small battle over the remainder of Jabba's possessions, and was the apparent winner. However, soon the mysterious [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr monks]] who inhabited the cellars removed his [[Brain/Legends|brain]] from his body and placed it in a [[B'omarr brain walker|spider-droid walker]], much as the monks themselves used.<ref name="Bib's Tale" />

Six months after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|events]] at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], a Twi'lek by the name of [[Firith Olan]] received Fortuna's messages that he'd been secretly sending and arrived on Tatooine to claim Jabba's treasures. Olan uncovered clues that an Imperial Agent by the name of [[Lirin Banolt]] knew of the final location of the missing [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class medium cruiser]], the [[Eidolon (Strike-class)|''Eidolon'']]. Olan knew that if he were to take possession of the ship, his personal power would increase greatly. However, the ''Eidolon'' was a fake&mdash;[[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] had a fake built and destroyed it while in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. The real purpose of the ''Eidolon'' was a hidden base on Tatooine, which Pestage could escape to.

Olan used Fortuna's computer skills to unlock the location of various weapons caches scattered over Tatooine and took control of at least 64 [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE Interceptors]]. [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] had been tasked by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]] with investigating events on Tatooine and uncovered the plot while enjoying the hospitality of [[Huff Darklighter]]. By this time, the Imperials began poking around led by [[Marl Semtin/Legends|Marl Semtin]] and destroyed Olan's TIE's. Olan tried to hide on Ryloth from his enemies and tried to abandon Fortuna on the planet but he stowed away on [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]' ship and returned to Tatooine.

Marl Semtin was tasked with securing the [[Eidolon Base]] and capturing Olan&mdash;he planned to put Olan in charge of the base given his underworld connections. Rogue Squadron attacked Eidolon Base, Olan panicked and Semtin stabbed him. Olan fled the base but ran right into Fortuna outside who took the wounded Twi'lek back to Jabba's Palace. He somehow convinced the monks to place his brain in the body of Olan, using the same techniques that got him in the walker in the first place.<ref name="X-wing Rogue Squadron: Battleground: Tatooine">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Battleground: Tatooine]]''</ref> Then with Olan's resources at his disposal along with the credits he embezzled from Jabba over the years, Fortuna began rebuilding Jabba's criminal empire, and continued on in the criminal underworld. In his new criminal empire, he met a young Twi'lek named [[Shiri'ani|Shrir'ani]], the protégé of Lady [[Valarian/Legends|Valarian]]. Becoming her lover, Fortuna turned Shrir'ani against Valarian.<ref name="Secrets of Tatooine">''[[Secrets of Tatooine]]''</ref> By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|Yuuzhan Vong war]], Fortuna created an alliance with Valarian to profit off of the invasion.<ref name="TNEGC" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|I make it my business to know things about people like you.|Bib Fortuna|<ref name="Agents of Deception">{{SWGTCG|set=Agents of Deception|scenario=Dark Side scenario campaign}}</ref>}}
[[File:BibFortuna_portrait-SWKIDS20.png|thumb|220px|Bib Fortuna was a tall, white-skinned Twi'lek.]]
Bib Fortuna was a tall, white-skinned Twi'lek with two thick [[Lekku/Legends|lekku]]<ref name="Oola's Tale" />&mdash;tentacular appendages that grew out of the back of his head&mdash;which he wore often draped over his shoulders for decorative effect.<ref name="ROTJN">''[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novel]]''</ref> His visage displayed a high bony crest, a knobby brow, bright,<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> scary<ref name="SWVD">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> red [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and a sharp<ref name="SWVD" /> fanged mouth.<ref name="Oola's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=A Time to Mourn, a Time to Dance: Oola's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref> The front of the neck displayed a large goiter, like many other male Twi'lek&mdash;including the ancient [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Kopecz]],<ref name="SW:JVS">''[[Star Wars: Jedi vs. Sith]]''</ref> the Imperial [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Boc Aseca]]<ref name="JK:DFII">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref> and the Rebel [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] pilot [[Nawara Ven]].<ref name="SWI59">{{InsiderCite|59|Who's Who in Rogue Squadron}}</ref> According to Twi'lek standards, Fortuna was considered "darkly elegant" and attractive, notably due to his thick lekku.<ref name="Oola's Tale" />

In addition to his native [[Twi'leki/Legends|Rylothean]],<ref name="Oola's Tale" /> Bib Fortuna also spoke [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], and he could at least understand [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]], the "common tongue" of the civilized [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="ROTJ" />

[[File:Bib_Fortuna_-_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|300px|Bib Fortuna, a slaver and spice trader turned majordomo|left]]
When he became Jabba's majordomo, Fortuna grew even more power-hungry. He came to believe he would acquire the wealth and influence necessary to conquer Ryloth and mold his fellow Twi'leks into the kinds of subjects the Empire valued&mdash;spies, bounty hunters and mercenaries. By saving his race from "exotic slavery," Bib Fortuna hoped he would bring back honor to his name and that of his ancestors.

Fortuna had been among the first to attract the attention of the Empire to Ryloth by selling ryll spice off-world. While he had thought the Twi'leks would adapt to life in the wider Empire, they did not. His own people had come to hate him utterly, but he still wished to bring them out of the horrors of slavery. He also performed a ritual of where he listed to himself each of the day's annoyances he had experienced every night before he slept.<ref name="Bib's Tale" />

==Equipment==
He often wore traditional black Ryloth<ref name="CharEnc">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> [[Robe/Legends|robe]]<nowiki/>s made from [[Jalavash worm silk]],<ref name="SWVD" /> which accentuated his natural paleness,<ref name="Malakili's Tale" /> along with half-[[Glove/Legends|glove]]<nowiki/>s and sliver<ref name="CharEnc" /> slaver<ref name="SWVD" /> [[Bracelet/Legends|bracelet]]<nowiki/>s. A pair of soft-soled shoes allowed the Twi'lek to walk down the corridors of Jabba's palace as silently as a wraith. He also kept a poisoned [[Dagger/Legends|dagger]] concealed in the folds of his robes.<ref name="SWVD" /> 

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:BibFortuna-NEGTC.png|thumb|150px|Bib Fortuna]]
In [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], Bib Fortuna was played by [[Michael Carter]] and voiced uncredited by the late [[Erik Bauersfeld]], who also voiced Admiral Ackbar in the film. For [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], [[Alan Ruscoe]] was initially cast to play the character in a scene in the Senate, but this scene was cut. He was later portrayed by [[Matthew Wood]] for his appearance on Tatooine.

Bib Fortuna actor Michael Carter, via an interview on [[TheForce.net|TheForce.Net]], has alluded to several cut scenes from ''Return of the Jedi'' that involved [[Jess/Legends|Jess]] and [[Salacious B. Crumb/Legends|Salacious B. Crumb]].<ref name="TFNinterview">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/mcarter.asp|text=TheForce.Net - Jedi Council - Interviews - Cellblock 1138 - Michael Carter|archivedate=20130217044710}}</ref> Some of these scenes appear in ''[["Lapti Nek": The Music Video from Jabba's Palace]]''.

During several scenes in ''Return of the Jedi'', Bib Fortuna can be heard speaking something which can be interpreted as a twisted form of English, suggesting that he spoke a heavy dialect of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]].

In earlier drafts of ''Return of the Jedi'', Fortuna's title was the High Beeser of Hoth.<ref name="Databank">{{DB|character|bibfortuna|Fortuna, Bib}}</ref>

Bib Fortuna's first words in ''Return of the Jedi'', "Die wanna wanga," are frequently quoted by underworld characters in ''Star Wars'' video games, most notably in [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast|''Jedi Outcast'']] and [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy|''Jedi Academy'']]. It is also said by [[Gragra/Legends|Gragra]] to [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] in ''The Phantom Menace''.

"[[Best Birthday Ever]]" says that his full name is Bib Oltwaxt Fortuna.

In the webcomic ''[[The Clone Wars: The Valsedian Operation]]'', a Twi'lek administrator was seen that resembled Bib Fortuna, although he was not identified. Tom Hodges later confirmed that the administrator was indeed intended to be Bib Fortuna.<ref name="email">{{EmailCite|email=File:HodgesReply.jpg|creator=[[Tom Hodges]]|date=2011-01-29}}</ref>

===LEGO Star Wars===
Fortuna has made several appearances in LEGO Star Wars media, including ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Out]]'', in which he attempts to sell R2-D2 and C-3PO cell phones,<ref name="LEGOESO">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Out]]''</ref> and [[LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace]].<ref name="LEGOTPM">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace]]''</ref> His most significant appearance is in [[The Phantom Clone]], an episode of ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles]]'', in which he is confronted and insulted by a reluctant C-3PO, encouraged by a group of Padawans.<ref name="LEGOTPC">{{YodaChronicles|The Phantom Clone}}</ref>
